rationale.f1: Provides background on which settings' curricula are and aren't reliably quality-assured; useful context but secondary to the collaboration/staff points.
rationale.f2: States that PRU-school collaboration is the answer to curriculum needs, matching the reference summary's core opening point directly.
rationale.f3: Ties funding shortfalls directly to a specific staffing gap (a dedicated educational psychologist), the core finance-and-recruitment link the reference summary highlights.
rationale.f4: States the core staff-recruitment problem (niche expertise hard to replace once lost), central to the recruitment-of-professional-staff theme.
rationale.f5: States that newly qualified teachers can't enter this provision and that pathways should be built into training, directly matching the reference summary's training-system point.
rationale.f6: Confirms the small-numbers/limited-training-access problem for this specialist workforce, supporting the recruitment theme.
rationale.f7: Describes a related capacity constraint (pulling staff out for training is hard), supporting but secondary to the core recruitment problem.
rationale.f8: Relates to consistent training coverage via statutory policy; touches the training theme but is more about mental-health provision generally than staff recruitment specifically.
rationale.f9: Lists broad recommendations including teacher training; relevant supporting context but diffuse relative to the specific recruitment/curriculum theme.
rationale.f10: States explicitly that this training should be embedded in initial teacher training, matching the reference summary's closing point almost verbatim.
rationale.f11: Concerns broader responsibility/funding for supporting excluded children generally, tangential to the specific special-education-curriculum and staff-recruitment theme.
rationale.f12: Explains how undiagnosed needs get children mislabeled and off-rolled, relevant to the special-education-needs identification issue but not to staff recruitment.
rationale.f13: A narrow, under-researched sub-topic (Welsh-medium EOTAS) that is tangential to the core curriculum-collaboration and recruitment themes.
rationale.f14: Describes vulnerability during the exclusion-to-EOTAS gap; relevant to special education support generally but not to curriculum collaboration or staff recruitment specifically.
rationale.r1: Ties the funding shortfall, staff-retention difficulty, and training-access problem together into a single root cause, the exact finance-and-recruitment link the reference summary describes.
rationale.r2: Connects embedding training in initial teacher training to the statutory whole-school approach, capturing the systemic argument behind the reference summary's training recommendation.
